title: ILLUSIONS

lists.name: (2) "The Causes, Bases, and Sources of Illusion"
lists.of: cause, basis, or source of illusion
items: 36 Hierarchy (multiplicity of confusable and interfering levels).
Misconstrual of function from appearance, Mis-supposition of appearance from function.
Poor or defective correlation of data, Mis-combined sensa or Percepts.
50 Deficiencies of fundamental knowledge: e.g. imprecise or undefined mathematics, geometry, physics, ethics, etc.
Pan-truth (misapplication of the doctrine so-named), Pan-paradoxy.
'Pseudo-convergences': e.g. In data series; Regressional fallacies.
55 Perspective: e.g. limited, fixed, specialized, or local; Defective coordinate systems or Coordinates.
Lack of a transcendent (to suggest imperfection, finitude, or the like) or a Companion.
Unwillingness to doubt or to consider the possibility of illusion; Complacency.

70 Fallacious equation of parvitude, rarity, singularity, etc with insignificance (e.g. discounting of what is small, exaggeration of the importance of what is large; erroneous proportionation of size to importance).
Monoideism (excessive preoccupation with a single, fixed idea).
Imperfections and Costs of common sense.
75 Pseudo-averaging (attempted averaging of what cannot be averaged)
